help: Build a calculation from retained revisions. Original rows, exact values, exclusions and input locations remain inspectable. Results are stored in a new dataset revision and can feed figures and publication tables.
exactHelp: Version 3 arithmetic uses exact fractions and bounded integer powers, including negative powers. Zero to the zeroth power is one. Quotient truncates toward zero; remainder preserves a = quotient ? divisor + remainder. Floor and ceiling round in the authored unit. Optional declared units validate dimensions and convert exactly; labels alone make no dimensional claim. Unknown conditions keep conditional values absent and exclude selected rows.
title: Result dataset title
joinHelp: Match rows by one or more exact keys. Only one right-hand row may match each key. Use a right-hand condition to choose the baseline stage. Unmatched rows either stop the calculation or retain absent values.
whereHelp: Rows outside the selection remain in the retained dataset with this exclusion reason. Their calculated cells are absent.
removeLast: Remove dependent calculation steps and joined datasets from the end first, so column references remain correct.
name: Output column name
invalid: Complete the input, matching keys, conditions, numerical calculations and declared units. Column names must be unique. Check missing values, division by zero and ambiguous matches.
previewNote: First five acquisition rows. The complete dataset is checked when you retain it.
columnWindow: Columns {first}?{last} of {total}. Selected columns remain available.
projectionHelp: Choose the input columns included in this calculation. Up to 256 input and result columns can be retained per calculation. Other source columns remain unchanged.
invalidColumn: Choose a column number within this dataset.
conditionBudget: Keep conditions within 8 nested levels and 64 nodes, with 2 to 16 conditions per group. This change was not applied.
algebraUpgradeHelp: This creates a new graph revision using exact domain algebra. Earlier graph revisions keep their original interpretation. Review the saved operation limits before enabling it; each input also keeps its own declared limits.
algebraHelp: Choose two earlier nodes with supported numerical domain declarations. Their declared namespace must match; labels do not define a field or coordinate system. No broadcasting or shape inference is performed. Source spellings and source references remain unchanged.
algebraShapes: Add and subtract require matching vector, matrix, complex or tensor shapes. Tensor addition and subtraction require explicit tensor support. Dot product requires equal-length vectors. Matrix product requires the left column count to equal the right row count. Multiply and divide apply to complex values; division by a zero complex value is refused.
algebraUnits: Uses declared unit definitions; units are never inferred from labels. Addition and subtraction convert compatible scales and offsets exactly, using the left unit (or the right absolute unit when adding a difference to an absolute value). Products compose dimensions canonically and require difference quantities. Without declared units, addition and subtraction require matching labels; products require empty labels. Incompatible shapes or units are refused without saving the edit.
algebraOperands: Choose two existing nodes that occur before this node, and a supported exact domain operation.
tensorUpgradeHelp: Save graph version 10 with explicit resource limits to use declared tensors and exact reshaping. Earlier graph revisions and results keep their original interpretation. Tensor arithmetic supports only addition and subtraction of equal shapes; no broadcasting or axis meaning is inferred.
reshapeHelp: Choose one earlier vector, matrix or tensor node and declare the complete target shape. The total component count must remain unchanged. Original source values and pinned references remain unchanged.
reshapeOrder: A vector has one dimension, a matrix two, and a tensor 3 to 16. Components retain their sequence with the last coordinate varying fastest. Reshaping does not transpose, reorder, broadcast or assign physical meaning to axes.
reshapeOperand: Choose a supported vector, matrix or tensor node that occurs before this node.
reshapeShapeInvalid: Enter exactly one dimension for a vector, two for a matrix, or 3 to 16 for a tensor. Every dimension must be a positive whole number and the total must fit exact indexing capacity.
graphWorking: Graph operation in progress. Please wait.
permuteUpgradeHelp: Create a new graph revision that supports explicit axis permutation. Review the saved operation limits before enabling it. Earlier graph revisions and retained results keep their original interpretation.
permuteHelp: Choose one earlier supported vector, matrix or tensor node. Enter every source axis exactly once, in the desired output order. Source values, nulls, declared context and pinned references are preserved.
permuteAxes: Source axes in output order (starting at 1, comma-separated)
permuteOrder: Each position in the list is an output axis; its number selects the source axis. For source shape [2, 3, 4], axes 3, 1, 2 give output shape [4, 2, 3]. Axes 1, 2, 3 keep that shape and component order unchanged. The rank and component count stay the same. No axis order or physical meaning is inferred.
permuteOperand: Choose a supported vector, matrix or tensor node that occurs before this node.
permuteAxesInvalid: List every source axis once, using whole numbers from 1 to the source rank, separated by commas. Include 1 to 16 axes without gaps, repeats or extra axes.
perCellUpgradeHelp: Create a graph revision that preserves each value’s exact or approximate computation, including mixed Pearson results. Earlier graph revisions and retained results keep their original interpretation.
alignmentUpgradeHelp: Create a new graph revision that supports explicit coordinate matching. Review the saved resource limits. Earlier graph revisions and retained results keep their original matching rules.
alignmentDirection-backward: Backward: right coordinate at or below left
alignmentDirection-forward: Forward: right coordinate at or above left
alignmentExcluded: Excluded right rows are skipped. Missing left coordinates follow the unmatched-row choice.
alignmentHelp: Select a scalar coordinate from earlier input bindings and a scalar column in the right dataset. Right coordinates must be nondecreasing within each equality-key partition in original source order. No sorting, interpolation or clock relationship is inferred. Equality keys are optional for this method; with no keys, all right rows form one partition.
alignmentUnits: Coordinates require compatible declared unit definitions. The tolerance is a nonnegative difference with a positive scale and zero offset. Coordinate selection is separate from any approximation in the selected payload.
alignmentInvalid: Choose both coordinates, a valid exact tolerance and its declared difference unit, plus explicit direction, tie and missing-coordinate choices. The draft has been preserved.
alignmentSourceMissing: Choose the retained right dataset before browsing its coordinate columns.
alignmentReceiptHelp: This receipt records the pinned coordinate matching decision. Payload computation is reported separately.
alignmentStatus-no-candidate: No candidate in the chosen direction
alignmentDelta: Candidate right coordinate minus left coordinate
alignmentDeltaUnit: Tolerance and signed coordinate difference use this declared difference unit.
